- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >1.0) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.0), model often overcorrects downward — adjust upward to avoid excessive bearish bias.  
- Model frequently underestimates upward price spikes in the 10–15 day horizon — apply a small upward bias (e.g., +0.5–1.5) to forecasts following strong positive sentiment.  
- Model tends to overestimate downward moves after recent spikes — apply a small downward bias (e.g., -0.5 to -1.0) to forecasts following strong negative sentiment.  
- Mean reversion is overestimated in short-term (1–3 day) forecasts — reduce forecast magnitude for immediate moves unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses the final 5–7 days — adjust last 5–7 forecast points upward if sentiment remains positive or downward if sentiment turns negative.
